# UK Postgraduate Funding for Indian Students — Verified Shortlist
*Researched 5 September 2026 from primary sources (Chevening, CSC/FCDO, British Council, Rhodes Trust, Gates Cambridge, Oxford, UKRI, Felix, Inlaks, JN Tata)*

## ⏰ Act now — two major deadlines within 6 weeks

| Scheme | Status | Deadline | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Chevening** | **OPEN** (since 4 Aug) | **6 Oct 2026, 11:00 UTC** | Full: tuition, stipend, flights |
| **Commonwealth Master's** | **Opens 8 Sept** (Tuesday) | **20 Oct 2026, 16:00 BST** | Full: tuition, £1,712/mo (£2,000 London), airfare, study-travel grant |

These two are your highest-value targets and they overlap — you can apply to both.

**Chevening eligibility (verified):** Indian citizenship, an undergraduate degree, **2 years / 2,800 hours work experience**, applications to **three** different eligible UK courses, and commitment to return to India for 2 years. It's leadership/impact-assessed, not need-based.

**Commonwealth Master's (verified):** India is confirmed on the eligible-country list. Requires at least a 2:1-equivalent undergraduate degree and — importantly — that you **"be unable to afford to study in the UK without this scholarship."** It's explicitly need-based and routed through a nominating body, so identify yours immediately.

## 🔬 Best fits for STEM specifically

**Gates Cambridge** — applications for 2027/28 open this month; deadlines **8 Dec 2026 or 6 Jan 2027** depending on course. Full funding, no nationality restriction, strong STEM cohort.

**Clarendon Fund (Oxford)** — 200+ fully funded awards. **No separate application**: you're automatically considered if you apply by Oxford's December/January course deadline. No restrictions on nationality or field; both master's and DPhil.

**Felix Scholarship** — Indian nationals only, at **Oxford, Reading and SOAS**. Full funding on merit *plus* financial need; requires a first-class bachelor's from an Indian university. Covers **all subjects except medicine**, so STEM and education both qualify. At Oxford there's no separate form — the January course deadline does it.

**UKRI studentships** — the standard route for funded PhDs. From 1 Oct 2026 the minimum stipend is **£21,805 (£23,805 London)**. ⚠️ **Critical caveat I'd flag:** UKRI states it only contributes **up to the home fee rate (£5,238)**, so as an international student you may have to cover the difference between home and overseas fees unless the university waives it. Always ask the supervisor/DTP directly whether the overseas differential is covered before investing in an application.

## 💷 Partial funding / fee waivers worth stacking

**GREAT Scholarships (British Council)** — **£10,000 towards tuition** for a one-year taught master's; India is eligible and the 2026-27 round ran 140+ awards across 60+ universities. Applications go **directly to the university**, deadlines vary, and the 2027-28 university list typically publishes around Nov/Dec. Good for topping up a self-funded or loan-funded plan.

**J.N. Tata Endowment** — a *loan* scholarship (partially convertible to a grant), open to **all disciplines**. Indian citizen, not over 45 as of 30 June 2026, minimum 60% at undergraduate level. Applications typically run roughly Dec/Jan–March.

**Commonwealth Shared Scholarships** — India is eligible and it's full funding for taught master's at selected universities, but the current cycle has closed. Next round expected around Dec 2026/Jan 2027 — set a reminder.

## ⚠️ Three corrections to widely circulated misinformation

1. **Commonwealth PhD Scholarships are NOT open to Indian nationals.** Many blogs and consultants still list this. The scheme has been restricted to **least developed countries and vulnerable states**, and the URL now redirects accordingly — India is not on the list. Don't waste a cycle on it.

2. **Inlaks Shivdasani has major subject exclusions that catch STEM applicants out.** It excludes **Computer Science**, Business/Finance/Management, and Medicine outright, and **Engineering & Natural Sciences are only considered at Imperial College London**. Also: Indian passport holder resident in India, **born on or after 1 Jan 1996**, minimum 70% for Maths/Sciences/Environment, and you must already hold an admission offer. If you're a CS applicant, Inlaks is a dead end regardless of merit.

3. **Rhodes India is closed for the 2027 cycle**, despite a site-wide banner reading "Applications for the Rhodes Scholarship 2027 are open!" That banner is generic; the India constituency page confirms it closed **23 July 2026** and reopens ~1 June 2027 for 2028 entry. Note also the hard age bar (18–23 on 1 October, or under 27 with a first degree completed on/after 1 Oct 2025) and a requirement of 4 of the last 10 years' study in India — this rules out many working professionals.

Separately, the CSC website carries an **active scam warning**. Legitimate schemes never charge application fees — treat any "Commonwealth Exchange Scholarship Council" or similar-sounding body as fraudulent, and apply only via `cscuk.fcdo.gov.uk`.

## Recommended action plan

**This week:** Draft Chevening essays and lock your three course choices (deadline is ~4 weeks out). Identify your Commonwealth nominating body before the 8 Sept opening.

**Sept–Oct:** Submit Chevening (6 Oct) and Commonwealth Master's (20 Oct).

**Nov–Dec:** Apply to Oxford/Cambridge courses by the December/January deadlines — this single action auto-enters you for **Clarendon** and **Felix**, and covers **Gates Cambridge** (8 Dec / 6 Jan). Highest effort-to-reward ratio available.

**Dec–Mar:** Watch for Commonwealth Shared Scholarships reopening, the GREAT 2027-28 university list, JN Tata, and Inlaks (if your subject qualifies).

**A strategic note:** the two strongest levers are that (a) Oxford and Cambridge applications automatically trigger consideration for several fully-funded awards at no extra cost, and (b) Chevening and Commonwealth use *different* selection logic — leadership/impact versus financial need — so a candidate weak on one can be strong on the other. Apply to both. One caveat on sequencing: Inlaks requires an admission offer in hand, whereas Chevening and Commonwealth do not, so don't hold back the latter two waiting on offers.
